label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I q.2 a.3…: Wherever things are more and less in some perfection…
locator: I q.2 a.3 co., quarta via: magis et minus dicuntur de diversis secundum quod appropinquant diversimode ad aliquid quod maxime est
interpretation: Read as the step the argument draws from it ('Est igitur aliquid quod est verissimum, et optimum, et nobilissimum'): where there are grades of a perfection, something is maximal in it. The maximum is read as having the perfection and as exceeded by nothing; the approach relation that grounds the comparatives is not formalized, and nothing makes the grades a measure. This is the premise an unbounded gradation would falsify (result AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-QUARTA-VIA, quartaViaNeedsMaximum); the reading follows the text and does not restrict it to transcendental perfections.
